title: Feedback transport-delay phase-margin budget
description: Allocate additional pure transport delay at an existing unity-gain crossover while retaining a requested phase margin.
formula: phase_loss = 360 f_c t_d; PM_remaining = PM_initial - phase_loss; t_max = (PM_initial - PM_target)/(360 f_c)
assumptions: Continuous-time SISO negative feedback; the undelayed closed loop is stable and has one relevant unity-gain crossover.
The added element is a pure time delay, with unit magnitude and phase -360 f t degrees; crossover frequency does not move.
Input phase margin already includes all existing plant, sensor and controller lag. Delay input is additional delay only.

A negative remaining margin or delay headroom is a failed design indication, not an invalid input. Multiple crossovers require checking every crossover separately; this calculator is not a global stability certificate.
Sampling, zero-order-hold magnitude, jitter, time variation and actuator saturation are not represented by a pure delay.

references.title: NASA NTRS: Time Domain Stability Margin Assessment, slides 4-6 and 12

constraints.message: A pure added delay cannot increase the original phase margin

title: Complex loop disturbance and measurement-noise sensitivity
description: Compute output-disturbance rejection and measurement-noise transmission from a measured complex return ratio at one frequency.
assumptions: SISO linear negative feedback with return ratio L measured without including the summing-junction minus sign.
The physical closed loop must be stable for sinusoidal steady-state amplitudes to apply; one complex frequency point cannot establish stability.
Disturbance is added at the plant output before the feedback pickoff; measurement noise is added only in the feedback measurement.
Disturbance and noise amplitudes use the same voltage convention, such as both RMS. Outputs are separate contributions, not their coherent or statistical sum.
The exact singular point L=-1 is excluded. Near this point the ideal linear model predicts large amplification, often beyond real actuator headroom.

references.title: Lehigh University ME450, Lecture 5: Classical Feedback Control, slides 13-15, equations 10-19

constraints.message: The singular return ratio L=-1 has no finite sensitivity

title: Phase-lead compensator at a chosen loop crossover
description: Place a lead compensator's peak phase boost at a selected crossover and normalize its gain using the uncompensated loop magnitude there.
formula: C(s)=Kc(1+s tau)/(1+s alpha tau); alpha=(1-sin(phi))/(1+sin(phi)); fz=fc sqrt(alpha); fp=fc/sqrt(alpha); Kc=sqrt(alpha)/M
assumptions: The requested positive phase boost is strictly between 0 and 90 degrees and is centered at the chosen crossover.
Plant magnitude includes all fixed gain and feedback sensing, but excludes the new lead compensator.
This design makes the local loop magnitude unity; plant phase, other crossovers and Nyquist stability still require separate assessment.
The controller is a continuous-time minimum-phase lead network. Finite amplifier bandwidth, component tolerances and high-frequency noise are not included.
No phase-margin-to-overshoot approximation is used. Peak boost approaching 90 degrees needs unbounded pole separation and high-frequency gain.

references.title: Toronto Metropolitan University: Introduction to Control Systems, section 13.2, equations 13-1 through 13-11
